analysis: Glycogen storage diseases are a group of inherited metabolic disorders characterized by the abnormal storage of glycogen due to enzyme deficiencies. Common examples include Pompe disease, McArdle disease, and von Gierke disease. In contrast, Krabbe's disease is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by a deficiency in the enzyme galactocerebrosidase, which leads to the accumulation of psychosine and is not related to glycogen metabolism. Similarly, Fabry's disease is a sphingolipidosis caused by a deficiency in the enzyme alpha-galactosidase A, also unrelated to glycogen storage. Fragile X syndrome is a genetic condition caused by a mutation in the FMR1 gene, which affects cognitive development and is not a metabolic disorder related to glycogen storage. Therefore, all the options listed (Krabbe's disease, Fabry's disease, and Fragile X syndrome) do not fall under the category of glycogen storage diseases. Hence, the correct answer is that all the options are not glycogen storage diseases.
